# LiteraryWorm - Ebooks and Audiobooks for the Whole Household

> LiteraryWorm is a reading and listening app: ebooks and audiobooks in one library, with a profile for each person at home (Kids and Teen profiles see only titles rated for them). It runs in any modern browser and installs as an app. Members pay monthly or yearly through Stripe and can cancel online at any time.

LiteraryWorm's full-text and audio library is public-domain classics: texts from Project Gutenberg and LibriVox recordings, including titles in French, German, Greek and Spanish. Members can also find almost any book through Google Books, keep it in their library, and upload their own DRM-free EPUBs (up to 20 at a time, each up to 50 MB), such as books they bought elsewhere, to read with their place, highlights and notes.

## Main Features

- **Reader and player**: highlights in twelve colours, notes, bookmarks, a dictionary, OpenDyslexic, a reading ruler and line focus; an audiobook player with a mini-player, a read-along transcript (for fifteen classics, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, Through the Looking-Glass, Frankenstein, Pride and Prejudice, A Christmas Carol, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, Treasure Island, Peter Pan, The War of the Worlds, The Jungle Book, Heart of Darkness, The Picture of Dorian Gray, The Secret Garden and The Call of the Wild, the book's own text marked as the LibriVox reader says it), sleep timer, bedtime listening (a dim view that sets the sleep timer and fades the sound out), car mode (big buttons that fill a phone or tablet screen, and voice control), Cast and listening on another device.
- **Household profiles**: up to 12 profiles (by plan), each with its own library, lists, goals, streaks and stats; PIN locks, daily limits and bedtimes; each profile can have its own monthly share of listening and natural-voice hours; a grown-up can turn natural voices on for a Kids profile; Kids profiles ask a grown-up for other books and can print a certificate for each badge and reading streak.
- **Book clubs**: spoiler-free discussion by chapter, AI discussion questions on the classics, polls on what to read next (LiteraryWorm titles or the owner's uploads), a year-together card each December and January, a reading schedule of chapters a week (members vote on the pace and the owner chooses), meetings with calendar files, shared highlights, listening along and where everyone is in the book. A club can read a LiteraryWorm title or a book its owner uploaded, found by title, author, ISBN or keywords and sorted by title, author, numbers or series; uploads stay private, and each member reads their own copy. Clubs reading an uploaded book can listen together, each member on their own copy at the same chapter.
- **Reading tools**: Didn't finish and Read again, moods and pace (with Feel-good picks on Discover), goals with rest days, reading plans to finish by a date, word and highlight review, badges, a Year in Review, imports and exports for Goodreads and StoryGraph, offline reading and scheduled offline listening. An opt-in Year in reading email each January sums up every profile's year.
- **AI help, labelled as AI**: book summaries, content notes, Ask the book, Translate, Who's who, Previously… recaps and book clubs' discussion questions written by Claude (Anthropic), never past the reader's place.
- **Browse**: 64 genres (Fantasy, Mystery, Romance, Classics, Poetry and LGBTQIA+ among them, plus every top-level Google Books subject, such as Cooking, Comics & Graphic Novels, Philosophy, Travel and True Crime, each showing only books filed under that subject) on Home, Discover and Search, with a row each for the brief's six and a profile's favourites. Visitors see a sample of 20 books on the home page; logged in, Keep discovering scrolls on through every genre. On adult profiles, Home's rows come from Open Library first, with Google Books as the fallback.
- **Search**: by title, author, keywords (descriptions, genres and series too) or ISBN, with keyword searches to try on Discover and Search. Members' own DRM-free uploads (EPUB .epub, PDF .pdf with real text, or Kindle .mobi, .azw3 and .azw; books with DRM can't be uploaded; read on their device) can be searched by title, author, keywords or ISBN, even inside their text, on their device. An upload can be listened to as well as read, with a voice from the member's own device, a natural voice from Google in the book's own language (English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Hindi, Arabic, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Swedish, Ukrainian, Tagalog, Bulgarian, Romanian or Greek; within a monthly allowance by plan: Basic 2 hours, Standard 6, Premium 12, with what's left shown in Account; parts played stay on the device for offline listening; with Character voices on, what the characters say is read by other voices, one per named speaker, in all 21 languages, and the listener can choose who reads whom and give each speaker their own speed; names it says wrongly can be respelled under Pronunciations; Voice the whole book keeps every part on the device ahead of time, on Wi-Fi; in the reader, Read aloud turns the pages with the voice and marks the word being spoken), or the LibriVox recording, read by a person, when the catalog has the same public-domain book. Members can also hear the public-domain classics in natural voices (first in the Voice menu, with character voices, previews and pronunciations; the LibriVox recording stays a choice), and change the voice and the characters' voices at any time from the player, the mini-player, the reader or a book club's page.
- **Sharing**: gift wishlists (a shared list can be given as a gift membership with its books), invite a friend (you each get a month free after their first payment, up to 2 months for inviting), reading sprints (a timed 15–30 minute session for a household or a book club, with everyone's pages at the end), buddy reads (a club for two), household challenges (books, hours, days or nine reading themes) and links to short clips of public-domain LibriVox recordings (or of an upload's natural voice, which play only for the member's household).
- **Languages and access**: the app in English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified), Korean, Hindi, Arabic, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Swedish, Ukrainian, Tagalog, Bulgarian, Romanian and Greek (the same 21 languages as the natural voices; Arabic right to left, with the whole layout mirrored; chosen in the accessibility menu, starting in the browser's language; the policies stay in English), with high contrast, larger text, wider text spacing, Lexend or OpenDyslexic for the whole app, and reduced motion; Continue on your phone shows a QR code that opens the same book at the same place; the menu scrolls on small screens.

## Pricing Information

- **[LiteraryWorm - Pricing](https://www.literaryworm.com/pricing)**: prices in US dollars, plus any applicable tax. A year costs ten months.
  - A first membership starts with 7 days free (nothing is charged if cancelled before they end).
  - Basic: $30.00/month or $300.00/year (1 profile, 5 hours of audiobooks a month, offline on 1 device)
  - Standard: $40.00/month or $400.00/year (up to 3 profiles, 30 hours a month, offline on 10 devices)
  - Premium: $60.00/month or $600.00/year (up to 12 profiles, unlimited audiobooks, offline on 24 devices)
- More natural-voice hours for members' uploads: 5 hours for $14.99 or 10 for $24.99, paid once, used after the month's plan hours and lasting 12 months.
- Gift memberships of 1, 3, 6 or 12 months, with up to 10 books to start with, gift cards of $25, $50 or $100 (credit for any plan, taken off the redeemer's charges; no cash value), and gifts of 5 or 10 natural-voice hours ($14.99 or $24.99) for a member's uploads.
- **Affiliate program** (/affiliates): approved members earn 20% of a referred member's first payment as account credit (no cash payouts), must disclose the commission and never market to children.
- **Try the demo** on the log-in page: a sample household kept in memory (books, clubs, a reading sprint, reading lists, highlights, a sample reader to follow, a reminder for a sample upcoming book, an invite link and a wishlist to give), which can't take payments.
